subject: PrivDeploy: network gating, procurement path, and day-zero checklist
messages:
From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@tidalhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-team@tidalhealth.com
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private hosting intake: VPC peering, procurement windows, and day-0 asks

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for taking time to chat last week. Tidal Health is moving forward with a private deployment for our inference workloads and we need to align on the following as part of our intake:

- VPC peering vs. private interconnect: we prefer a transit/VPN approach initially, but need guidance on recommended NAT/egress pattern for PHI workloads.
- Procurement timing: our purchasing lead wants an estimate for reserved capacity start date and any invoice milestones.
- Day‑0 runbook: we need a short checklist (network ACLs, service account/service principal creation, TLS cert handoff, KMS integration) so our infra team can prepare.

I attached a rough VPC sketch and a scoping sheet exported from our internal ticket. Can you confirm what documents your finance/procurement team needs to start SOW/PO issuance?

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Cole
Director of Cloud Ops, Tidal Health
---
Attachments: tidal_vpc_topology_sketch.pdf (diagram), privdeploy_scoping_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@tidalhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting intake: VPC peering, procurement windows, and day-0 asks

Hi Samantha —

Appreciate the packet, that helps. Quick answers below and a concise day‑0 checklist appended. Ben and Lauren are looped for procurement and the activation cadence.

1) Network pattern: for PHI we typically recommend a private interconnect where available (ExpressRoute/Direct Connect) with a failover VPN. If you must use transit/VPN initially, please plan for dedicated egress subnets and NAT instances per tenant, and restrict outbound egress to our allowed API IP ranges (see Drive link I’ll share).

2) Procurement timing: Ben — can you confirm the usual cadence for reserved capacity contracts (monthly vs. seasonal start) and the required billing documents? Tidal indicated they want a target start by 2027-05-15.

3) Day‑0 checklist (high level):
   - Create service account: redwood-privdeploy-<tidal>-svc with IAM roles: compute.admin (limited), kms.encrypt/decrypt, network.viewer
   - TLS cert: provide SAN list and preferred CA (we support Let's Encrypt for non-PHI, for PHI we recommend customer-managed certs via KMS/HSM)
   - KMS: share key ARN or contact to integrate with our key-wrap process; if customer manages key, we require proof of rotation policy
   - Firewall/NACLs: allow inbound from bastion IPs and provisioning ports (TCP 22, 443, custom 33770 for runtime control); restrict outbound to our registry and model catalog endpoints
   - Routing: ensure route table entry to our peering CIDR 10.250.0.0/16 (example) and confirm MTU >= 1500
   - Audit: enable flow logs to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket and share read-only ARN/roles for evidence collection

I’ll upload a concise one‑page Day‑0 runbook to the Drive folder; Ben, Lauren — if you can reply with procurement path and any PO template expectations, that would be great.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Manager, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@tidalhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting intake: VPC peering, procurement windows, and day-0 asks

Thanks Karthik / Samantha —

Procurement notes and timeline:
- Reserved capacity contracts: standard lead time is 2–4 weeks from signed PO to capacity reservation, faster if we already have cleared quota in the target region.
- Billing docs: we need a signed SOW (we'll draft), a PO referencing SOW id DH-2027-1192, and the billing contact + remit address. For health customers we typically request net-30 with SOC2 clause inserted; exceptions can be evaluated by finance.
- Start target 2027-05-15 looks reasonable if PO is in place by 2027-04-20. If Tidal needs earlier, we can provision initial burst capacity on hosted pool and then transition to Dedicated.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Redwood to send SOW draft by Tue 2027-03-30.
2) Tidal to confirm PO timeline and provide billing contact by Mon 2027-04-11.
3) Karthik/Infra to confirm quota in the requested region and post provisioning window.

I attached a short procurement checklist template we use for PO submission. I’ll also open a HubSpot deal stage update.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Sales, Enterprise Accounts | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: procurement_submission_template.pdf
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@tidalhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting intake: VPC peering, procurement windows, and day-0 asks

Hi all —

Confirming receipt and next steps from an onboarding/ops readiness perspective:
- Karthik: please slide the one‑page Day‑0 runbook into the shared Drive folder by EOD Mon (that will let Tidal ops start checklist items).
- Samantha: please add the billing contact and preferred PO template to the Drive folder (we'll use Ben's template if you don't have a preferred one).
- I'll schedule a 30‑minute kickoff with our activation engineer and Tidal infra for Wed 2027-04-13 (I’ll propose 10:00 PT) to walk Day‑0 items and wire up access.

Small ask on evidence: if Tidal can pre-provide a sample network ACL and a S3/GCS bucket ARN for flow logs, we can pre-validate perms before day‑zero and shorten the activation window.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the line.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
